Discern

dih-SURN -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, SURN. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To discern to perceive a thing clearly.

In the crowded photograph, she could just discern her grandmother's face in the back row.

Worked Example

Two paintings hang side by side, and to most visitors they are identical. The restorer looks for ten seconds, then points: the brushwork in the left-hand corner changes direction, and the varnish is a shade warmer on one canvas than on the other.

The restorer can discern the difference -- perceive clearly what others cannot see at all. Discern usually carries a sense of effort or skill: the thing really is there, but it takes attention to pick it out.

How Discern Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

detect

detect: notice something that is not obvious

distinguish

distinguish: tell one thing apart from another

perceive

perceive: become aware of something through the senses or the mind

Antonyms

overlook

overlook: fail to notice something

confuse

confuse: mistake one thing for another

How Strong Is It? — detect → discern → distinguish

detect vs. discern

detect vs. discern: Detect only says you noticed something was there -- a smoke alarm detects smoke -- while discern says you made it out clearly enough to know what it was.

distinguish vs. discern

distinguish vs. discern: Distinguish always needs two things to hold apart, while discern needs only one: you discern a shape in the fog, but you distinguish the twin on the left from the twin on the right.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — dis-

prefix — dis-: apart (Latin)

root — cern-

root — cern-: to separate, to sift (Latin cernere)

Put it together

Put it together: Discern joins Latin dis- ('apart') with cernere ('to separate, to sift'). The Romans pictured sifting grain: shaking the whole pile until one thing separates out from the rest. To discern is to sift the world with your eyes or your mind until the thing you are after stands apart.

Use the root in a new word: secret

Use the root in a new word: secret: The recipe was a family secret, kept in a locked tin for sixty years.

Root Check

Word Choice

Discern works for the senses and for the mind alike: discern a figure in the mist, discern a pattern in the data, discern someone's real motive. It nearly always implies the thing was hard to make out. Do not confuse it with discrepancy, a noun about facts that fail to match -- the two words look alike but are completely unrelated.
